Barkley can sleep through a fire truck but not through a cheese wrapper opened two rooms away.
He greets every dog at Runyon by name. The names are ones he assigned.
Barkley treats an open door as a formal invitation and a closed door as a clerical error.
He has been told no roughly four thousand times and has yet to find the argument persuasive.
Barkley’s tail has two settings: off, and structural concern.
He once barked at a leaf for eleven minutes. The leaf has not fallen since.
Barkley has never been caught. He has been observed, photographed and named — but never caught.
He is deeply suspicious of the mailman, the skateboard and one specific bush.
Barkley can find the only sunbeam in a crowded room and will lie in it regardless of who was there first.
His résumé lists “available” under both skills and interests.
Barkley considers the vacuum a rival rather than an appliance. The vacuum has declined to comment.
He keeps a mental list of everyone who has ever given him cheese. It is the only thing he has never forgotten.
